proposals.label: Krab et al. (2020)
proposals.rationale: Krab et al. (2020) describe the largest RAD21 cohort so far: 49 individuals from 33 families, including 24 new cases. The entry lacks feature frequencies, several new features (hearing loss, heart defects, cleft palate, vertebral and foregut anomalies, choanal and anal atresia, behavioral profile, postnatal microcephaly) and many variants not in the variant table (e.g., C585R, R586X, F600del, L603P, S345P, P376R, I206Tfs*3, G547Afs*65, T461I, R65Q). The paper also adds genotype-phenotype data comparing microdeletions with intragenic variants, molecular modeling, and evidence that familial transmission is common.

paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) reported 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations, including 24 previously unpublished cases. The patients came from Australia, Europe, Turkey, Canada, and the United States. Full clinical information was available for 29 individuals from 22 families (cohort A), all of whom had CdLS clinical scores of at least 5. Compared with the phenotype caused by NIPBL or SMC1A variants, the phenotype was attenuated, with milder facial morphology, limb anomalies, cognition, and behavior. Frequent features were short nose (23/26), long and/or smooth philtrum (26/29), concave nasal ridge (24/29), thick eyebrows (20/24), long eyelashes (21/26), synophrys (19/28), thin upper lip vermilion (23/29), short fifth finger (23/28), postnatal microcephaly (16/28), and gastroesophageal reflux (13/25). No patient had major limb malformations (0/29) or visual impairment (0/24). Small hands (5/27), small feet (3/27), hirsutism (10/26), and seizures (2/22) were less common than in the NIPBL and SMC1A cohorts. Hearing loss was present in 8/24 patients, heart defects in 9/23, and cleft palate in 6/25. Pregnancies and births were usually normal and prenatal growth retardation was uncommon; short stature and microcephaly developed after birth. About half of the patients had congenital anomalies. Unusual findings included vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae) and malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut. Diaphragmatic hernia, anal atresia, or choanal atresia occurred occasionally. Sixteen of 29 patients (55%) had normal or mildly impaired cognition, and none had severe or profound disability. All patients aged 3 years and older used some words, and problems were mainly language-based. Behavioral problems were present in 14 of 25 (56%), mainly anxiety, ADHD, autistic features, and obsessive-compulsive behavior. Self-injurious behavior (1/18) and aggression (1/16) were infrequent.

paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) identified 31 different RAD21 alterations in 33 families. These comprised 7 unique deletions, 6 of which also included other genes, and 24 intragenic sequence variants. Of the sequence variants, 13 were predicted to be truncating (2 nonsense, 2 splice site, and 9 frameshift) and were scattered throughout the gene. Three were in-frame deletions, and the missense variants tended to cluster at the protein-binding domains. Two variants were recurrent: a c.1753T-C transition resulting in a cys585-to-arg (C585R) substitution, and a c.1756C-T transition resulting in an arg586-to-ter (R586X) substitution. C585R arose de novo in 1 previously reported patient and was found in 2 relatives in a new family. Molecular dynamics modeling predicted that C585R destabilizes the RAD21-SMC1A domain by causing the adjacent arg586 to lose its salt-bridge contact with glu577. R586X was found in 2 previously unpublished families; in one family it was inherited from the father, who was also affected, and facial morphology differed between the families.

paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) reported further RAD21 variants in CdLS patients. In a previously unpublished patient with classic CdLS and no variants in other known CdLS genes on a targeted gene panel, they found an in-frame deletion, c.1800_1802del, resulting in deletion of phe600 (F600del). Modeling showed no structural effect, but the authors considered the variant likely pathogenic on the basis of the phenotype. In a previously reported patient, they found a de novo c.1808T-C transition resulting in a leu603-to-pro (L603P) substitution; modeling predicted that pro603 bends the alpha helix and moves lys605 out of its position near ATPase site 1. In a DECIPHER patient, they found a de novo c.1033T-C transition resulting in a ser345-to-pro (S345P) substitution. Modeling predicted that S345P impairs the interaction between RAD21 and STAG1/2 by creating a new curved alpha-helix segment that separates from the STAG2 surface. In contrast, the previously reported de novo c.1127C-G transversion, resulting in a pro376-to-arg (P376R) substitution, was predicted to form a new salt bridge that over-stabilizes the RAD21-STAG2 interaction. Other previously unpublished heterozygous variants were 2 de novo frameshifts, c.617_620del (Ile206ThrfsTer3) and c.1635del (Gly547AlafsTer65), and a paternally inherited c.1382C-T transition resulting in a thr461-to-ile (T461I) substitution. The authors also included a c.194G-A transition resulting in an arg65-to-gln (R65Q) substitution, which was listed in ClinVar as a variant of uncertain significance. Based on phenotype, modeling, and the literature, they considered R65Q and T461I likely pathogenic, possibly acting through altered phosphorylation motifs or PDS5 interaction.

paragraphs.text: Compared with patients carrying intragenic variants, Krab et al. (2020) observed a trend toward higher CdLS scores and more frequent growth impairment in patients with microdeletions. They found no difference in major malformations or in cognitive and behavioral problems. CdLS scores did not differ between truncating and nontruncating sequence variants. Variability within and between families was striking, especially in cognition and behavior, and in most families it could not be explained by mosaicism.

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations (24 different intragenic sequence variants and 7 unique microdeletions), including 24 previously unpublished cases, from Australia, Europe, Turkey, Canada and the United States. Full clinical information was available for 29 individuals from 22 families (cohort A). All of them had CdLS clinical scores of at least 5. Their phenotype was an attenuated CdLS phenotype compared with that caused by NIPBL or SMC1A variants, with milder facial morphology, limb anomalies, cognition and behavior.
quotes: We gathered a series of 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations [24 different intragenic sequence variants (2 recurrent), 7 unique microdeletions], including 24 hitherto unpublished cases.
Their phenotype is an attenuated CdLS phenotype compared to that caused by variants in NIPBL or SMC1A for facial morphology, limb anomalies, and especially for cognition and behavior.
All patients in cohort A (age range 0–61 years, median 9 years, mean 18 years; 15 males) had CdLS scores of at least five, sufficient to warrant molecular genetic testing for CdLS.

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found that in the 29 cohort A patients with RAD21 variants, the frequent features were short nose (23/26), long and/or smooth philtrum (26/29), concave nasal ridge (24/29), thick eyebrows (20/24), long eyelashes (21/26), synophrys (19/28), thin upper lip vermilion (23/29), short fifth finger (23/28), postnatal microcephaly (16/28) and gastroesophageal reflux (13/25). No patient had major limb malformations (0/29) or visual impairment (0/24). Small hands (5/27), small feet (3/27), hirsutism (10/26) and seizures (2/22) were less common than in the NIPBL and SMC1A cohorts. Hearing loss was present in 8/24, heart defects in 9/23 and cleft palate in 6/25.
quotes: Postnatal head circumference < − 2SD | HP:0000252 | 16/28 | 57 | 23/36 | 64 | 54/62 | 87
RAD21 patients less frequently have increased body hair (hirsutism, bushy eyebrows, low scalp hair lines), major limb malformations are not reported, and hands and feet are generally of normal size.

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found that cognitive functioning and behavior were attenuated in RAD21 patients: 16 of 29 (55%) had normal or mildly impaired cognition, none had severe or profound disability, and all patients aged 3 years and older used some words. Problems were mainly language-based. Behavioral problems were present in 14 of 25 (56%), mainly anxiety, ADHD, autistic features and obsessive-compulsive behavior. Self-injurious behavior (1/18) and aggression (1/16) were infrequent.
quotes: The majority of RAD21 patients (16/29, 55%) have normal or mildly impaired cognitive functioning (SMC1A group 32%; NIPBL group 7%)
Still, all RAD21 patients aged 3 years and above were able to use some words.
14/25 RAD21 patients (56%) with sufficiently available information on behavior had problems, mainly features of anxiety, ADHD, ASD, and obsessive–compulsive behavior.

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported that in RAD21 patients pregnancies and births were usually normal and prenatal growth retardation was uncommon. Short stature and microcephaly developed after birth. About half had congenital anomalies such as cleft palate and cardiac anomalies. Unusual findings included vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae) and malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut. Diaphragmatic hernia, anal atresia or choanal atresia occurred occasionally.
quotes: The natural history data from the present study indicate that pregnancies and birth tend to progress normally, prenatal growth retardation being present in a small minority. About half of the patients have congenital anomalies (cleft palate; cardiac anomalies).
Unusual anomalies in the RAD21 cases are vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae).
Malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut are relatively frequent in RAD21 patients and have only rarely been described in CdLS

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) suggested, from limited data on cohort B, that biallelic RAD21 variants can cause Mungan syndrome and monoallelic RAD21 variants can cause holoprosencephaly, with or without CdLS characteristics. In several further cases, including cases with sclerocornea, it was uncertain whether the RAD21 variant was involved.
quotes: In the 20 individuals with limited clinical information, additional phenotypes include Mungan syndrome (in patients with biallelic variants) and holoprosencephaly, with or without CdLS characteristics.

The (limited) available information of individuals from cohort B suggests that biallelic RAD21 variants can also lead to Mungan syndrome and monoallelic RAD21 variants to holoprosencephaly (like one case in cohort A) and possibly schizophrenia

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found 31 different RAD21 alterations in 33 families: 7 unique deletions (6 of which also included other genes) and 24 intragenic sequence variants. Of the sequence variants, 13 were predicted to be truncating (2 nonsense, 2 splice site and 9 frameshift) and were scattered throughout the gene, 3 were in-frame deletions, and the missense variants tended to cluster at the protein-binding domains. Two variants were recurrent (p.Cys585Arg and p.Arg586*). Nine of 21 index cases with known inheritance had familial variants.
quotes: The 33 families harbor 31 different variants: seven unique copy number variations (CNVs) and 24 intragenic sequence variants.
A relatively large proportion of the cases are familial (nine out of 21 index cases for whom inheritance could be established).
Of the 24 different sequence variants, 13 are predicted be truncating (2 nonsense, 2 splice site and 9 frameshift variants), and these are scattered throughout the gene.

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported a recurrent RAD21 missense variant, c.1753T>C (p.Cys585Arg), in 2 families: it arose de novo in 1 previously reported patient and was found in 2 relatives in a new family. Molecular dynamics modeling predicted that Cys585Arg destabilizes the RAD21-SMC1A domain by causing the adjacent Arg586 to lose its salt-bridge contact with Glu577.

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported a recurrent RAD21 nonsense variant, c.1756C>T (p.Arg586*), in 2 previously unpublished families. In one family it was inherited from the father, who was also affected. Facial morphology varied between the families carrying this variant.

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found a de novo in-frame deletion in RAD21, c.1774_1776del (p.Gln592del), in a previously reported patient with a CdLS score of 8. Molecular dynamics simulation predicted that loss of Gln592 distorts an alpha helix and moves Lys605 away from ATPase site 1 of the SMC1A/SMC3 head, disturbing the cohesin cycle.
quotes: F17 | Gudmunsson 2019 | Updated | 8 | Exon 14 | c.1774_1776del | p.(Gln592del) | Inframe deletionb | De novo
This situation promotes a conformational change in the alpha helix, causing the Lys605, which is placed in the same alpha helix, to move away from site 1 of the ATPase.

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found a RAD21 in-frame deletion, c.1800_1802del (p.Phe600del), in a previously unpublished patient with classic CdLS who had no variants in other known CdLS genes on a targeted gene panel. Modeling did not show a structural effect, but the authors considered the variant likely pathogenic based on the phenotype.
quotes: F18 | Unpublished | New | 9 | Exon 14 | c.1800_1802del | p.(Phe600del) | Inframe deletionb |

Although the Phe600del variant does not seem to affect RAD21 structure, it leads to a classical CdLS phenotype without variants in additional known CdLS genes (using a targeted gene panel). Thus, it does seem likely pathogenic.

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found a de novo RAD21 missense variant, c.1808T>C (p.Leu603Pro), in a previously reported patient in cohort B. Modeling predicted that Pro603 bends the alpha helix and moves Lys605 out of its position near ATPase site 1.

Presence of mutated Pro603 instead of wild-type Leu603 promotes a local change in the bending angle of the alpha-helix in which it is located, resulting in a conformational change in the alpha helix that moves Lys605 out of its initial position close to ATPase site 1

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found a de novo RAD21 missense variant, c.1033T>C (p.Ser345Pro), in a DECIPHER patient. Modeling predicted that it impairs the interaction between RAD21 and STAG1/2 by creating a new curved alpha-helix segment that separates from the STAG2 surface. The previously reported de novo variant c.1127C>G (p.Pro376Arg) was predicted to form a new salt bridge that over-stabilizes the RAD21-STAG2 interaction.

The Ser345Pro variant impairs RAD21 and STAG1/2 interactions due to promotion of a de novo curved small alpha-helix segment that binds to the pre-existing alpha helix, which separates from the surface of STAG2.
Nevertheless, Pro376Arg does promote the formation of a new salt bridge between RAD21 and STAG2, which is predicted to cause over-stabilization of the interaction between the two proteins.

evidence.statement: Krab et al. (2020) updated the family with Mungan syndrome in which 3 sibs were homozygous for the RAD21 variant c.1864G>A (p.Ala622Thr). Modeling showed no structural alteration. proposals.rationale: This paper is the first in the entry to describe RAD21 deficiency caused by germline chromothripsis. It was resolved by nanopore long-read sequencing and produced a contiguous deletion of RAD21 and EXT1 that spared TRPS1, with reduced RAD21 expression. It also adds features the entry does not yet list: congenital heart defect, cleft palate, thoracic scoliosis, butterfly vertebrae, umbilical hernia and multiple exostoses. It also compares 6 patients with RAD21/EXT1 deletions.

paragraphs.text: Lei et al. (2020) described a 6-year-old Han Chinese boy, the first child of healthy unrelated parents, who had a de novo t(8;18)(q22;q21) translocation. He had growth retardation (height and weight -2.0 SD), mild-to-moderate intellectual disability, left-sided cleft palate, and a congenital heart defect (ventricular septal defect, double-outlet right ventricle, and juxtaposition of the aorta and pulmonary artery). Other features were thoracic scoliosis, butterfly vertebrae, fifth-finger clinodactyly, fingerpads, umbilical and inguinal hernias, and recurrent respiratory infections. Facial dysmorphism included arched thick eyebrows, long eyelashes, a depressed nasal bridge, anteverted nostrils, large prominent ears, dental malocclusion, and micrognathia. Kabuki syndrome was initially suspected. Multiple exostoses were found at age 10 years.

paragraphs.text: Lei et al. (2020) used nanopore long-read sequencing and the dnarrange pipeline to study a boy with features of CdLS4 and Langer-Giedion syndrome. They showed that his de novo t(8;18) translocation was germline chromothripsis: the genome had been shattered into 19 fragments (15 from chromosome 8 and 4 from chromosome 18) that rejoined in random order and orientation. The rearrangement caused 4 deletions on chromosome 8 (456, 1,957, 520, and 3,529 kb) and 1 deletion on chromosome 18 (1,528 kb), all consistent with array results. One chromosome 8 deletion contained RAD21 and EXT1 but not TRPS1. Earlier short-read whole-genome sequencing had not resolved the rearrangement, and no pathogenic variants were found in the Kabuki syndrome genes.

evidence.statement: Lei et al. (2020) described a 6-year-old Han Chinese boy, the first child of healthy unrelated parents, who had a de novo t(8;18)(q22;q21) translocation. He had growth retardation (height and weight -2.0 SD), mild-to-moderate intellectual disability, left-sided cleft palate, and a congenital heart defect (ventricular septal defect, double-outlet right ventricle, and juxtaposition of the aorta and pulmonary artery). He also had thoracic scoliosis, butterfly vertebrae, fifth-finger clinodactyly, fingerpads, umbilical and inguinal hernias, recurrent respiratory infections, and facial dysmorphism including arched thick eyebrows, long eyelashes, a depressed nasal bridge, anteverted nostrils, large prominent ears, dental malocclusion, and micrognathia. Kabuki syndrome was initially suspected, and multiple exostoses were found at age 10 years.
quotes: He was the first child of healthy, unrelated parents of Han-Chinese origin with unremarkable family history, with a karyotype of 46,XY,t(8;18)(q22;q21)dn (Fig. 1a).

He had mild-to-moderate ID, congenital heart defect (ventricular septal defect, right ventricle double exit, aorta, and pulmonary artery juxtaposition), thoracic scoliosis, butterfly vertebra (T5, T8, T10, and T12), clinodactyly of fifth fingers, fingerpads, umbilical hernia (left side), inguinal hernia, recurrent respiratory infections
He was found to have multiple exostoses in his right leg, left calf and shoulder blade at the age of 10 years.

evidence.statement: Lei et al. (2020) used nanopore long-read sequencing and the dnarrange pipeline in this patient. The de novo t(8;18) translocation turned out to be germline chromothripsis: the genome had been shattered into 19 fragments (15 from chromosome 8 and 4 from chromosome 18) that rejoined in random order and orientation. The rearrangement caused 4 deletions on chromosome 8 (456, 1,957, 520, and 3,529 kb) and 1 deletion on chromosome 18 (1,528 kb), all of which were consistent with array results. One chromosome 8 deletion contained RAD21 and EXT1 but not TRPS1. Earlier short-read whole-genome sequencing had not resolved the rearrangement, and no pathogenic variants were found in the Kabuki syndrome genes.
quotes: The patient genome was evidently shattered into 19 fragments, and rejoined into derivative chromosomes in a random order and orientation.
The rearrangement involves four large deletions from chr8 (456, 1,957, 520, and 3529 kb) and one large deletion from chr18 (1528 kb) (Fig. 2b, yellow rectangles).
We noted that one deletion from chr8 contained disease associated genes, RAD21 and EXT1 (Figs. 3a, S4).

evidence.statement: Lei et al. (2020) found reduced RAD21 and EXT1 expression on quantitative RT-PCR of the patient's lymphoblastoid cells, while TRPS1 expression was unchanged. They concluded that loss of RAD21 and EXT1 explained the phenotype, a likely contiguous gene syndrome combining CdLS4 and atypical Langer-Giedion syndrome. They considered involvement of other disrupted genes, including ZFPM2, unlikely.
quotes: Real-time PCR results from the LCLs of the patient showed decreased gene expression of RAD21 (OMIM 606462) and EXT1 (OMIM 608177) but not TRPS1 (OMIM 604386) (Fig. 3b, Table S5).

These two genes could fully explain the disease phenotype with facial dysmorphisms and bone abnormality, which is likely a contiguous gene syndrome, Cornelia de Lange syndrome type IV (CdLs-4) and atypical Langer-Giedion syndrome (LGS), also known as trichorhinophalangeal syndrome type II (TRPSII).

evidence.statement: Lei et al. (2020) compared their patient with 5 previously reported patients who had Langer-Giedion syndrome with deletions that included RAD21 and EXT1 but spared TRPS1. The 6 patients shared overlapping features: arched thick eyebrows (6 patients), long eyelashes (5), depressed or broad nasal bridge (5), sparse scalp hair (4), and intellectual disability (4 of 6). Only their patient had thoracic scoliosis and a congenital heart defect. Because 2 of 8 previously reported patients with RAD21 variants had congenital heart disease, the authors suggested that RAD21 deficiency might be responsible for the heart disease.
quotes: Interestingly, five patients with Langer–Giedion syndrome without TRPS1 gene disruption have been reported (Fig. 3a). Consistent with our patient, all five patients have deletions involving RAD21 and EXT1.
In addition to these symptoms, our patient had thoracic scoliosis and congenital heart defect, which were not described in the five patients previously reported.
It is possible that RAD21 defect might be responsible for this patient’s congenital heart disease.
